findings.evidence: `Representation/SemisimplePoint.lean:68` defines `IsSemisimplePoint` on the same `WithConv (H →ₐ[k] K)` point type, while this file defines `IsUnipotent` at line 73.
findings.fix: Rename it to `IsUnipotentPoint` and consistently rename its associated declarations to the `isUnipotentPoint_*`/`IsUnipotentPoint.*` family.
findings.issue: `HopfAlgebra.IsUnipotent` omits `Point`, unlike the adjacent point-action predicate `HopfAlgebra.IsSemisimplePoint`, making the namespace API ambiguous with the general-linear predicate.

findings.evidence: `JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:122` has `IsSemisimple.mul_of_commute`, and `Representation/SemisimplePoint.lean:171` has `IsSemisimplePoint.mul_of_commute`; both expose the same commuting-product hypothesis.
findings.fix: Rename both declarations to `IsUnipotent.mul_of_commute` (and, after the predicate rename, `IsUnipotentPoint.mul_of_commute`).
findings.issue: `IsUnipotent.mul` hides the essential `Commute g h` hypothesis; the exact adjacent convention names such closure results `mul_of_commute`. The same issue occurs for the point lemma at `Unipotent/Point.lean:129`.

summary: The point predicate and commuting-product lemmas diverge from adjacent canonical naming.
